summary: Frontend Playwright suite executed end-to-end against the deployed preview URL. All 14 required scenarios passed: landing render, navbar+hero+pricing CTAs to /signup and /signin, signup→/dashboard with welcome heading containing the user email, dashboard stats cards, logout (cookies cleared + protected route redirects to /signin on revisit), admin signin (admin@promptai.app), wrong password stays on /signin with error toast, ProtectedRoute redirect for /dashboard when logged out, newsletter submit (toast, no reload), contact form submit (success toast + fields cleared), FAQ accordion expand/collapse, and Pricing Pro CTA navigates to /signup. No JS exceptions / pageerrors. The 401 console messages observed are the expected unauthenticated GET /api/auth/me probe from AuthContext on mount and are not regressions.
critical_code_review_comments: Consider suppressing the /api/auth/me 401 console noise (catch and treat as anonymous) so a logged-out landing page has a clean console — purely cosmetic, not a bug.
AuthShell, Input, Divider, GoogleMark are imported from `@/pages/SignIn` inside SignUp.jsx — this couples two pages. Moving shared auth UI into /components/auth/ would be cleaner.
test_credentials: admin@promptai.app / Admin@PromptAI2025 (worked). Fresh signup used ui-test-<ts>@example.com / TestPass1234! (worked).
seed_data_creation: Created one transient user via signup flow (ui-test-<unix_ts>@example.com), one newsletter row (news-<ts>@example.com), one contact row (Ada Lovelace / contact-<ts>@example.com). Safe to leave or purge.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All 14 landing+auth+dashboard frontend flows are green on the preview URL. Iteration 1 backend fixes (logout cookie clear + tokens_valid_from invalidation, email-only brute-force key) are confirmed effective via UI behavior: protected /dashboard redirects to /signin immediately after logout. If retesting, reuse the same data-testids; ProtectedRoute redirects on 401; sonner toasts render via [data-sonner-toast]. The /api/auth/me 401 on landing is expected (not a bug).
